data.name: Sergian
data.long_meaning: The name Sergian comes from the Greek word 'sergios' which means 'rule of the serpent'. This name was borne by several early Christian saints, including Saint Sergius of Radonezh who is revered as the patron saint of Russia. Sergius is often depicted holding a cross with two serpents entwined around it, symbolizing the power of Christ over evil.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of Christ over evil.

in_hebrew.name: סרגיאן
in_hebrew.meaning: משרתו של סרגיוס, או שומר של סרגיוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם סרגיאן הוא שם פרטי שמקורו ביוונית ופירושו משרתו של סרגיוס, או שומר של סרגיוס. השם סרגיוס עצמו מקורו בלטינית ופירושו שומר או משרת. השם נמצא בשימוש הנוצרי בימי הביניים ומשויך לקדושים ולמאמינים.

in_greek.name: Σεργιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σεργιανός προέρχεται από το ελληνικό όνομα Σέργιος και σημαίνει υπηρέτης του Σεργίου ή φύλακας του Σεργίου. Το όνομα Σεργιος ελήφθη από τη λατινική λέξη Sergius, που σημαίνει φύλακας ή υπηρέτης. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν δημοφιλές στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία και συσχετίζεται με πολλούς αγίους.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sergian can be traced back to the Greek language and the early Christian era. Saints Sergius and Bacchus, known as the "Tutors of the Roman Empire," were a popular subject of Christian art and devotion during the medieval period. The depiction of Saint Sergius with serpents has been a powerful symbol of the triumph of good over evil, and has influenced various forms of art, literature, and folklore.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sergian holds a deep spiritual significance as a reminder of the transformative power of faith and the victory of Christ over sin and evil. The symbol of the serpent is intricately connected to the story of the Garden of Eden and the Fall of Adam and Eve. However, in the context of the Christian saints named Sergius, the serpent symbolizes deliverance, healing, and the transformative power of God. This name continues to inspire and challenge individuals to embrace their faith and trust in the power of the cross to bring about spiritual transformation and victory over the challenges of life.

historical_references.reference: According to tradition, St. Sergius and St. Bacchus were Roman soldiers who were martyred during the persecution of Diocletian in the late 3rd century. They are believed to have converted many people to Christianity in the Roman army, and their feast day is celebrated on September 24.

Sergius of Reshaina (circa 411-464 AD) was a prominent Syrian physician, philosopher, and theologian. He is notable for his role in the Council of Chalcedon in 451 AD, where he defended the orthodox Christian view of the two natures of Christ (divine and human).

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sergian, derived from Saint Sergius of Radonezh, is seen in various modern contexts. In the realm of Russian Orthodoxy, it is a popular name for boys. In military history, there are references to the Sergian of Russia Order, which is the highest order of chivalry in the Russian Orthodox Church. In fantasy literature, especially in Slavic and Russian mythology-based works, Sergian is a common name for strong, brave and powerful characters. This name holds a deep historical and cultural significance in Slavic and Russian traditions.
